clauses.normalized_text: This specification describes an optimized expression of the semantics of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), referred to as HTTP version 2 (HTTP/2).
clauses.raw_text: This specification describes an optimized expression of the semantics of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), referred to as HTTP version 2 (HTTP/2).

clauses.normalized_text: HTTP/2 enables a more efficient use of network resources and a reduced latency by introducing field compression and allowing multiple concurrent exchanges on the same connection.
clauses.raw_text: HTTP/2 enables a more efficient use of network resources and a reduced latency by introducing field compression and allowing multiple concurrent exchanges on the same connection.

clauses.normalized_text: This document obsoletes RFCs 7540 and 8740.
clauses.raw_text: This document obsoletes RFCs 7540 and 8740.

clauses.normalized_text: The performance of applications using the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP, [HTTP]) is linked to how each version of HTTP uses the underlying transport, and the conditions under which the transport operates.
clauses.raw_text: The performance of applications using the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP, [HTTP]) is linked to how each version of HTTP uses the underlying transport, and the conditions under which the transport operates.

clauses.normalized_text: Making multiple concurrent requests can reduce latency and improve application performance.
clauses.raw_text: Making multiple concurrent requests can reduce latency and improve application performance.

clauses.normalized_text: HTTP/1.0 allowed only one request to be outstanding at a time on a given TCP [TCP] connection.
clauses.raw_text: HTTP/1.0 allowed only one request to be outstanding at a time on a given TCP [TCP] connection.

clauses.normalized_text: HTTP/1.1 [HTTP/1.1] added request pipelining, but this only partially addressed request concurrency and still suffers from application-layer head-of-line blocking.
clauses.raw_text: HTTP/1.1 [HTTP/1.1] added request pipelining, but this only partially addressed request concurrency and still suffers from application-layer head-of-line blocking.

clauses.normalized_text: Therefore, HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1 clients use multiple connections to a server to make concurrent requests.
clauses.raw_text: Therefore, HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1 clients use multiple connections to a server to make concurrent requests.

clauses.normalized_text: Furthermore, HTTP fields are often repetitive and verbose, causing unnecessary network traffic as well as causing the initial TCP congestion window to quickly fill.
clauses.raw_text: Furthermore, HTTP fields are often repetitive and verbose, causing unnecessary network traffic as well as causing the initial TCP congestion window to quickly fill.

clauses.normalized_text: This can result in excessive latency when multiple requests are made on a new TCP connection.
clauses.raw_text: This can result in excessive latency when multiple requests are made on a new TCP connection.

clauses.normalized_text: HTTP/2 addresses these issues by defining an optimized mapping of HTTP's semantics to an underlying connection.
clauses.raw_text: HTTP/2 addresses these issues by defining an optimized mapping of HTTP's semantics to an underlying connection.

clauses.normalized_text: Specifically, it allows interleaving of messages on the same connection and uses an efficient coding for HTTP fields.
clauses.raw_text: Specifically, it allows interleaving of messages on the same connection and uses an efficient coding for HTTP fields.

clauses.normalized_text: It also allows prioritization of requests, letting more important requests complete more quickly, further improving performance.
clauses.raw_text: It also allows prioritization of requests, letting more important requests complete more quickly, further improving performance.

clauses.normalized_text: The resulting protocol is more friendly to the network because fewer TCP connections can be used in comparison to HTTP/1.x.
clauses.raw_text: The resulting protocol is more friendly to the network because fewer TCP connections can be used in comparison to HTTP/1.x.

clauses.normalized_text: This means less competition with other flows and longer-lived connections, which in turn lead to better utilization of available network capacity.
clauses.raw_text: This means less competition with other flows and longer-lived connections, which in turn lead to better utilization of available network capacity.

clauses.normalized_text: Note, however, that TCP head-of-line blocking is not addressed by this protocol.
clauses.raw_text: Note, however, that TCP head-of-line blocking is not addressed by this protocol.

clauses.normalized_text: Finally, HTTP/2 also enables more efficient processing of messages through use of binary message framing.
clauses.raw_text: Finally, HTTP/2 also enables more efficient processing of messages through use of binary message framing.

clauses.normalized_text: Note: This list was assembled from the set of registered TLS cipher suites when [RFC7540] was developed.
clauses.raw_text: Note: This list was assembled from the set of registered TLS cipher suites when [RFC7540] was developed.

clauses.normalized_text: This list includes those cipher suites that do not offer an ephemeral key exchange and those that are based on the TLS null, stream, or block cipher type (as defined in Section 6.2.3 of [TLS12]).
clauses.raw_text: This list includes those cipher suites that do not offer an ephemeral key exchange and those that are based on the TLS null, stream, or block cipher type (as defined in Section 6.2.3 of [TLS12]).

clauses.normalized_text: Additional cipher suites with these properties could be defined; these would not be explicitly prohibited.
clauses.raw_text: Additional cipher suites with these properties could be defined; these would not be explicitly prohibited.

clauses.normalized_text: For more details, see Section 9.2.2.
clauses.raw_text: For more details, see Section 9.2.2.

clauses.normalized_text: This revision includes the following substantive changes:
clauses.raw_text: This revision includes the following substantive changes:

clauses.normalized_text: Use of TLS 1.3 was defined based on [RFC8740], which this document obsoletes.
clauses.raw_text: * Use of TLS 1.3 was defined based on [RFC8740], which this document obsoletes.

clauses.normalized_text: The priority scheme defined in RFC 7540 is deprecated.
clauses.raw_text: * The priority scheme defined in RFC 7540 is deprecated.

clauses.normalized_text: Definitions for the format of the PRIORITY frame and the priority fields in the HEADERS frame have been retained, plus the rules governing when PRIORITY frames can be sent and received, but the semantics of these fields are only described in RFC 7540.
clauses.raw_text: Definitions for the format of the PRIORITY frame and the priority fields in the HEADERS frame have been retained, plus the rules governing when PRIORITY frames can be sent and received, but the semantics of these fields are only described in RFC 7540.

clauses.normalized_text: The priority signaling scheme from RFC 7540 was not successful.
clauses.raw_text: The priority signaling scheme from RFC 7540 was not successful.

clauses.normalized_text: Using the simpler signaling in [HTTP-PRIORITY] is recommended.
clauses.raw_text: Using the simpler signaling in [HTTP-PRIORITY] is recommended.

clauses.normalized_text: The HTTP/1.1 Upgrade mechanism is deprecated and no longer specified in this document.
clauses.raw_text: * The HTTP/1.1 Upgrade mechanism is deprecated and no longer specified in this document.

clauses.normalized_text: It was never widely deployed, with plaintext HTTP/2 users choosing to use the prior-knowledge implementation instead.
clauses.raw_text: It was never widely deployed, with plaintext HTTP/2 users choosing to use the prior-knowledge implementation instead.

clauses.normalized_text: Validation for field names and values has been narrowed.
clauses.raw_text: * Validation for field names and values has been narrowed.

clauses.normalized_text: The validation that is mandatory for intermediaries is precisely defined, and error reporting for requests has been amended to encourage sending 400-series status codes.
clauses.raw_text: The validation that is mandatory for intermediaries is precisely defined, and error reporting for requests has been amended to encourage sending 400-series status codes.

clauses.normalized_text: The ranges of codepoints for settings and frame types that were reserved for Experimental Use are now available for general use.
clauses.raw_text: * The ranges of codepoints for settings and frame types that were reserved for Experimental Use are now available for general use.

clauses.normalized_text: Connection-specific header fields -- which are prohibited -- are more precisely and comprehensively identified.
clauses.raw_text: * Connection-specific header fields -- which are prohibited -- are more precisely and comprehensively identified.

clauses.normalized_text: Host and ":authority" are no longer permitted to disagree.
clauses.raw_text: * Host and ":authority" are no longer permitted to disagree.

clauses.normalized_text: Rules for sending Dynamic Table Size Update instructions after changes in settings have been clarified in Section 4.3.1.
clauses.raw_text: * Rules for sending Dynamic Table Size Update instructions after changes in settings have been clarified in Section 4.3.1.

clauses.normalized_text: Editorial changes are also included.
clauses.raw_text: Editorial changes are also included.

clauses.normalized_text: In particular, changes to terminology and document structure are in response to updates to core HTTP semantics [HTTP].
clauses.raw_text: In particular, changes to terminology and document structure are in response to updates to core HTTP semantics [HTTP].

clauses.normalized_text: Those documents now include some concepts that were first defined in RFC 7540, such as the 421 status code or connection coalescing.
clauses.raw_text: Those documents now include some concepts that were first defined in RFC 7540, such as the 421 status code or connection coalescing.
